fields.name: French Bulldog
fields.description:
The French Bulldog, affectionately known as the "Frenchie," is a small, muscular companion breed with a compact build, signature bat-like ears, and a smooth, short coat. Weighing up to about 28 pounds, these charming dogs feature a distinctive flat face, wrinkled expression, and alert, curious demeanor.
Frenchies are playful, affectionate, and adaptable, thriving as loving lap dogs that bond closely with their families. They're smart yet sometimes stubborn, generally good with children and other pets when socialized, and prefer a relaxed lifestyle over intense exercise—a short daily walk or play session keeps them content.
Their clownish personality, snorts, and endearing underbite make them one of the most popular and charismatic small breeds today.

fields.name: Labrador Retriever
fields.description:
The Labrador Retriever is one of the world's most popular and beloved breeds—a medium-to-large, sturdy, athletic dog with a friendly, outgoing, and gentle temperament. Known for their intelligence, eagerness to please, and exceptional trainability, Labs excel as family companions, service dogs, guide dogs, search-and-rescue workers, and hunting retrievers.
They come in three classic colors: black, yellow, and chocolate, with a short, dense, water-resistant double coat and an otter-like tail. Labs are energetic and love water, fetching, and play—requiring regular exercise and mental stimulation to prevent boredom. They're famously patient and tolerant with children, other pets, and strangers, making them ideal family dogs when given proper training and activity.
Their cheerful, affectionate nature and "happy tail" wagging have earned them a spot as the ultimate friendly companion breed.

fields.name: Jack Russell Terrier
fields.description:
The Jack Russell Terrier is a small, energetic, and fearless working terrier bred for fox hunting. Compact yet powerfully built (typically 10–15 inches tall, 13–17 pounds), these dogs feature a distinctive white coat with black, tan, or brown markings, expressive dark eyes, and erect V-shaped ears. Their broken, smooth, or rough coat is easy to maintain.
Jack Russells are intelligent, bold, and full of personality—often described as big dogs in small bodies. They're highly active, requiring lots of exercise, mental stimulation, and outlets for their digging, chasing, and prey-drive instincts to prevent boredom or mischief. Loyal and affectionate with family, they can be strong-willed and need consistent, positive training and early socialization.
Their endless enthusiasm, speed, and joyful spirit make them perfect for active owners who love adventure and play.

fields.name: Beagle
fields.description:
The Beagle is a small-to-medium-sized hound breed famous for its cheerful personality, exceptional sense of smell, and classic tricolor (or bicolor) coat. Standing 13–15 inches tall (with a slightly larger variety up to 16 inches), these compact, sturdy dogs feature long droopy ears, soulful dark eyes, a broad head, and a white-tipped tail often carried high.
Beagles are friendly, outgoing, and merry—great with families, children, and other dogs when socialized. Their strong hunting instincts and love of following scents make them curious explorers who can be food-motivated and prone to "selective hearing" when a interesting smell appears. They need regular exercise, mental stimulation (like scent games), and secure fencing to prevent wandering.
Their musical howl (or "bay"), playful nature, and affectionate demeanor have made them enduring favorites as family pets and scent-detection dogs.

fields.name: Shih Tzu
fields.description:
The Shih Tzu is a small, charming companion breed with a regal history as a lap dog of Chinese royalty. Typically weighing 9–16 pounds and standing 8–11 inches tall, these dogs are known for their long, flowing double coat (often in various colors like gold, white, black, or particolor), expressive round eyes, pushed-in face, and distinctive topknot often tied with a bow.
Shih Tzus are affectionate, outgoing, and playful—true "lion dogs" in personality, loving attention and thriving as devoted family pets. They're generally good with children and other animals when socialized, though their brachycephalic (flat-faced) structure makes them sensitive to heat and overexertion. They need moderate exercise (short walks and indoor play) but excel in a relaxed home environment.
Regular grooming is essential to prevent matting, and their cheerful, cuddly nature makes them one of the most endearing toy breeds.

fields.name: Siberian Husky
fields.description:
The Siberian Husky is a medium-sized, athletic working breed originally bred by the Chukchi people of Siberia for pulling sleds over long distances in harsh Arctic conditions. Known for their striking appearance—thick double coat (often gray-and-white, black-and-white, or red-and-white), erect triangular ears, bushy tail, and captivating almond-shaped eyes that can be blue, brown, or heterochromatic—these dogs exude elegance and wild spirit.
Huskies are friendly, outgoing, and gentle, with a high energy level and strong pack mentality. They're intelligent but independent, sometimes stubborn, and not typically the best choice for novice owners due to their escape-artist tendencies and love of running. They thrive with plenty of exercise (ideally including pulling or long runs), mental challenges, and a secure yard—cold weather is their favorite. While affectionate with family, they may not be overly clingy and can be vocal with dramatic "talking" howls rather than barks.
Their endurance, beauty, and playful wolf-like charm make them a favorite for active owners who appreciate their adventurous nature.

fields.name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
fields.description:
The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a small, sturdy herding breed with a big personality and iconic "fox-like" appearance. Standing 10–12 inches tall and weighing 25–30 pounds, these low-to-the-ground dogs feature a long body, short legs, large erect ears, and a foxy face. Their double coat comes in red, sable, fawn, black & tan, or tricolor—often with white markings—and a docked or naturally bobbed tail.
Pembrokes are intelligent, alert, and affectionate, known for their cheerful, outgoing nature and strong loyalty to family. They're energetic and playful, with a herding instinct that can show as nipping at heels—making early training and socialization essential. They need regular exercise (walks, play, or agility) and mental stimulation to stay happy and prevent mischief.
Famous for their "Queen's favorite" status and adorable waddle, Pembrokes bring endless charm, sass, and love to active households.

fields.name: Doberman Pinscher
fields.description:
The Doberman Pinscher is a sleek, powerful, and elegant working breed developed in Germany for personal protection. Medium-to-large in size (60–100+ pounds, 24–28 inches tall), these dogs boast a muscular, athletic build, short glossy coat (classically black & rust, with red, blue, or fawn variations possible), cropped or natural ears, and a distinctive alert, wedge-shaped head with intense expression.
Dobermans are highly intelligent, fearless, and loyal—often forming deep bonds with their family while remaining wary of strangers, making them excellent guard dogs. They're energetic, athletic, and quick learners, thriving on challenging training, obedience work, protection sports, or vigorous exercise like running and agility. With proper socialization and firm, consistent leadership, they're affectionate, playful, and gentle with loved ones, including children.
Their striking appearance, unwavering courage, and velcro-like devotion have made them iconic as both protectors and cherished companions.

fields.name: Chihuahua
fields.description:
The Chihuahua is the world's smallest dog breed, a tiny yet bold companion originating from Mexico. Weighing just 2–6 pounds and standing 5–8 inches tall, these pocket-sized dogs come in smooth or long-coated varieties and a wide range of colors (fawn, black, chocolate, cream, etc.). They feature a distinctive "apple-shaped" head, large expressive eyes, erect ears, and a confident, saucy expression.
Chihuahuas are feisty, lively, and fiercely loyal—often forming intense bonds with one person while being wary of strangers. They're alert, vocal (quick to bark at anything unusual), and surprisingly brave, sometimes acting like big dogs despite their size. They need minimal exercise (short walks and indoor play suffice) but benefit from early socialization and positive training to curb potential nippy or territorial behavior. Sensitive to cold, they love laps, warmth, and attention.
Their big personality in a tiny package makes them ideal for apartment living and devoted owners who appreciate their sassy charm.

fields.name: Bernese Mountain Dog
fields.description:
The Bernese Mountain Dog is a large, powerful, and strikingly beautiful working breed from the Swiss Alps, historically used for farm work, drafting, and guarding. Weighing 80–115 pounds and standing 23–28 inches tall, these gentle giants feature a long, silky tri-color coat (jet black with rust and white markings), a broad head, expressive dark eyes, and a friendly, calm expression.
Berners are known for their sweet, affectionate, and loyal nature—devoted family companions who are patient with children and generally good with other pets when socialized. They're calm indoors but need moderate daily exercise (walks, play, or carting in cooler weather) and thrive in cooler climates due to their thick double coat. Early training and socialization help channel their strength and prevent shyness.
Their "gentle giant" temperament, love of snow, and soulful eyes make them cherished pets for families seeking a loving, majestic companion—though their shorter lifespan (7–10 years) is a noted consideration.

fields.name: Golden Retriever
fields.description:
The Golden Retriever is a medium-to-large, friendly, and versatile sporting breed beloved worldwide for its sunny disposition and golden wavy coat. Weighing 55–75 pounds and standing 21–24 inches tall, these dogs feature a dense, water-repellent double coat in rich golden shades, expressive dark eyes, floppy ears, and a broad, smiling face.
Goldens are intelligent, eager to please, and highly trainable—excelling as family pets, service dogs, therapy dogs, guide dogs, and hunting retrievers. They're outgoing, gentle, and patient, typically great with children, other pets, and strangers alike. Energetic and playful, they love water, fetching, and outdoor adventures, needing regular exercise and mental stimulation to stay happy and well-behaved.
Their affectionate, loyal nature, "happy tail" wags, and willingness to cuddle have made them one of the most popular and trusted companion breeds.

fields.name: Samoyed
fields.description:
The Samoyed is a stunning, medium-sized spitz breed originating from Siberia, historically used by nomadic Samoyede people for herding reindeer, pulling sleds, and keeping warm at night. Weighing 35–65 pounds and standing 19–23.5 inches tall, these dogs are instantly recognizable by their thick, fluffy pure-white (or biscuit) double coat, fox-like face, erect triangular ears, dark almond-shaped eyes, and signature "Sammy smile"—an upturned mouth that gives them a perpetually happy expression.
Samoyeds are friendly, gentle, outgoing, and affectionate—excellent family companions who love people, including children, and often get along well with other pets. They're intelligent and playful but can be independent or stubborn, with a strong pack instinct and tendency to vocalize (howls and "talk"). They need regular exercise (walks, play, or cold-weather activities), mental stimulation, and thorough grooming to manage heavy shedding ("Samoyed snow"). Thriving in cooler climates, they're energetic yet adaptable with proper outlets.
Their cloud-like fluff, endless smiles, and loving nature make them one of the most photogenic and joyful breeds around.

fields.name: Pug
fields.description:
The Pug is a small, charming companion breed with an ancient history as a favored lap dog of Chinese emperors and European royalty. Weighing 14–18 pounds and standing 10–13 inches tall, these sturdy, square-proportioned dogs are famous for their wrinkled face, short muzzle, large round eyes, velvety ears, and tightly curled tail. They come in classic fawn (with black mask) or solid black, with a short, smooth, double coat that's easy to groom.
Pugs are affectionate, playful, and mischievous—true clowns who love attention, cuddles, and being the center of family life. They're generally good with children and other pets when socialized, though their flat face makes them prone to snoring, breathing issues, and heat sensitivity (short walks in cool weather are best). Intelligent but sometimes stubborn, they respond well to positive training and thrive indoors with moderate exercise and lots of love.
Their expressive faces, comical antics, and devoted "shadow" personality make Pugs one of the most endearing and instantly recognizable toy breeds.

fields.name: Border Collie
fields.description:
The Border Collie is a medium-sized, highly intelligent herding breed widely regarded as the smartest dog in the world. Standing 18–22 inches tall and weighing 30–55 pounds, these agile athletes feature a medium-length double coat (smooth or rough) most commonly in black & white, with other colors like blue merle, red, or tricolor possible. They have a distinctive intense "stare," alert prick or semi-prick ears, and a streamlined, athletic build built for speed and endurance.
Border Collies are energetic, focused, and work-obsessed—bred to control sheep with precision using their famous "eye" and crouching stance. They're extremely trainable, eager to learn, and excel in agility, obedience, flyball, herding trials, and other dog sports. With family, they're affectionate and loyal but need massive daily exercise (physical and mental) to prevent boredom-driven behaviors like chewing or herding kids/pets. Early socialization and consistent training are key for their strong work drive.
Their unmatched intelligence, boundless energy, and mesmerizing herding ability make them ideal for active, experienced owners who can provide purpose and stimulation.

fields.name: German Shepherd
fields.description:
The German Shepherd is a large, versatile, and highly intelligent working breed, originally developed in Germany for herding and guarding sheep. Standing 22–26 inches tall and weighing 50–90 pounds, these powerful dogs feature a strong, muscular build, a distinctive sloping back, erect ears, and a bushy tail. Their medium-length double coat is most commonly black and tan (saddle pattern), though sable, black, or white variations exist.
German Shepherds are confident, courageous, steady, and deeply loyal—often forming strong bonds with their family while remaining naturally protective and alert. Renowned for exceptional trainability and work ethic, they excel in police, military, search-and-rescue, service, and protection roles. They need consistent training, firm but fair leadership, and plenty of physical and mental exercise (daily runs, training sessions, or tasks) to stay balanced and prevent boredom or destructive behavior. With proper socialization, they’re typically good with children and can be gentle despite their imposing presence.
Their noble appearance, sharp mind, and unwavering devotion have made them one of the most respected and iconic breeds worldwide.
